name: ground lentil pie
instructions:
A pot pie built on the same umami DNA as Nisha Vora's [[lentil-wellington]] — mushroom + walnut + miso + nutritional yeast + lentil base — but restructured as a POT PIE (filling in a pie plate under a crust) with a specific set of dried/powdered/heavy-cream modifications that give it a distinct character. Less production than the wellington (no forming the log, no pre-baking, no braiding); a simpler weeknight-friendly execution.

The core moves that distinguish this from Nisha's original:
- ONION POWDER (not fresh diced onion)
- DRIED HERBS (not fresh — DRIED DILL for anglican direction, DRIED TARRAGON for french direction)
- NO TOMATO PASTE (replaced by worcestershire/tamarind for anglican, or dijon mustard for french)
- BUTTER (not olive oil) as the fat
- HEAVY CREAM to hydrate the filling before baking
- PUREED CELERY pulsed with the mushrooms
- FRESH CRUSHED GARLIC added LATE (not sautéed) — keeps a raw-garlic bite

See HAZARD note in the notes section for WHY all of these modifications belong together as a set.

SERVES 6-8. 9 1/2-inch deep-dish pie plate.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

Crust:
- 1 single-crust pie dough (or panko topping — see [[turnip-yam-pie]] for the pot pie format alternatives)
- 1 large egg (for egg wash if using pie crust)
- 1 tsp water

Filling:
- ~1/3 cup (60g) dried brown or green lentils (~6 oz cooked)
- 2 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp vegetable oil
- 1-2 tsp onion powder (NOT fresh diced onion — see HAZARD note)
- 6 garlic cloves, CRUSHED (side of knife or garlic press) — reserved for LATE addition, not the sauté
- 8 oz mushrooms (shiitake + cremini mix is default), pulsed with:
- ~2 stalks celery, pulsed WITH the mushrooms
- 1 tsp dried thyme (or 1 tbsp fresh)
- HERB PICKER (see DIRECTIONAL PICKERS note): 1 tsp DRIED DILL (anglican) OR 1 tsp DRIED TARRAGON (french) — or both
- 1 tsp sweet or hot paprika (optional)
- freshly cracked black pepper
- 1 tsp kosher salt
- 1 cup (~110g) walnuts, TOASTED, ground to fine crumbs (see [[lentil-wellington]] TOASTED WALNUTS note — same rule applies here)
- 2 tbsp light miso paste
- 2 tbsp nutritional yeast
- DEPTH/TANG PICKER (see DIRECTIONAL PICKERS note): 1-2 tbsp worcestershire sauce and/or tamarind paste (anglican) OR 1-2 tbsp dijon mustard (french)
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1/4 cup (~20g) panko breadcrumbs
- 1/4 cup (32g) all-purpose flour
- 3-4 tbsp heavy cream (stirred in LATE to hydrate the filling — biggest upgrade, see HEAVY CREAM note)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. COOK THE LENTILS: instant pot (2/3 cup water + pinch salt, high 6 min, natural release 10 min) or stovetop (cover with water, boil then simmer 20-30 min until tender-not-mushy). Drain any excess. Refrigerate until cool.

2. TOAST + GRIND WALNUTS: skillet on medium-low 3-5 min tossing frequently OR oven 8-10 min at 350°F. Cool slightly. Pulse in food processor to fine crumbs — DON'T over-process into walnut butter.

3. PULSE MUSHROOMS + CELERY TOGETHER: put the mushrooms AND ~2 stalks of celery in a food processor. Pulse until finely chopped. The celery disappears into the background and gives the filling a vegetal-savory bass note.

4. SAUTÉ THE MUSHROOM-CELERY MIX: melt butter + vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Stir in onion powder and cook 30 seconds (it blooms quickly — don't scorch). Add the pulsed mushroom+celery mixture, dried thyme, DRIED DILL or DRIED TARRAGON (or both), paprika, black pepper. Cook ~5-7 min stirring occasionally until the mushrooms have released their liquid and it has mostly evaporated. Add 1 tsp salt and cook 1 more min. Transfer to fridge to COOL COMPLETELY.

5. PREHEAT OVEN to 400°F.

6. MAKE THE FILLING BASE: in a food processor, combine the cooled lentils + cooled mushroom-celery mixture + miso + nutritional yeast + worcestershire/tamarind (or dijon mustard) + lemon juice. Blend until somewhat smooth and coming together.

7. ADD THE ABSORBERS: add the ground toasted walnuts, panko, and all-purpose flour to the processor. Blend again until well incorporated. Transfer the filling to a bowl.

8. LATE ADDITIONS — CRUSHED GARLIC + HEAVY CREAM:
   - Stir in the CRUSHED FRESH GARLIC (raw, not sautéed) — it keeps some bite this way, which carries the finished pie.
   - Stir in 3-4 tbsp HEAVY CREAM. The filling should read moist but hold its shape — not wet-runny. Add more cream a splash at a time if it's still dry.

9. ASSEMBLE: transfer the filling to a 9 1/2-inch deep-dish pie plate on a foil-lined baking sheet. Even out the surface. Top with the chilled pie crust (fluted edge, four 2-inch oval vents cut in the center); brush with egg wash + pinch of salt. OR: skip the pie crust and top with panko + oil spray for a lighter presentation (see [[turnip-yam-pie]] TOPPING VARIATION note).

10. BAKE at 400°F for ~30 min until the crust is deeply golden and the filling is bubbling around the edges. Rest 10 min before slicing.
notes:
A pot-pie restructuring of Nisha Vora's Lentil Wellington ([[lentil-wellington]]) — same lentil + mushroom + walnut + miso + nutritional yeast umami base, but with a set of load-bearing modifications that push the dish into either an anglican or french register (both work) and simplify the production down to a pot pie format.

=== INSPIRATION + EXPERIMENTAL PROGRESS ===

This recipe started as a variant of Nisha Vora's [[lentil-wellington]] (Rainbow Plant Life) and evolved into its own thing after a few rounds of cooking. Worth documenting the arc — each step below was a real experiment with a real result.

1. STARTED WITH NISHA'S ORIGINAL. Fresh onion, tomato paste, fresh rosemary, olive oil, wellington log-in-braided-pastry format. Worked great — filling read unmistakably meaty despite being fully plant-based; the mushroom + toasted walnut + miso + nutritional yeast + tomato paste umami stack does the job. The only 'issue' was that it read distinctly CONTEMPORARY-VEGAN — heavy on the vegan-glutamate-additions register, cleanly good but recognizably a 2020s-vegan dish rather than a british or french holiday classic.

2. FIRST DEPARTURE — ANGLICAN REGISTER. Swapped olive oil for BUTTER + vegetable oil (classical english fat, pulls dish away from mediterranean); swapped tomato paste for WORCESTERSHIRE + TAMARIND (anglican umami condiment stack); swapped fresh rosemary for DRIED DILL (dill is at home in british / northern-european cooking). Reads distinctly more british-holiday-wellington — closer to the classical beef-wellington heritage the format descends from.

3. DISCOVERED HAZARD — HAMBURGER-Y READ. First attempt at the anglican direction kept fresh diced onion + tomato paste and just added dill. Result: the three-way combination of FRESH DILL + TOMATO PASTE + FRESH ONIONS pushed the loaf into a distinctly HAMBURGER-LOAF-WITH-KETCHUP register — diner meatloaf, not british wellington. Fine flavor in the abstract; wrong flavor for what the dish was trying to be.

4. RESOLUTION — THE SWAPS BELONG TOGETHER AS A UNIT. Realized all three had to move together: ONION POWDER (not fresh) + DRIED HERBS (not fresh) + NO TOMATO PASTE (worcestershire/tamarind or mustard instead). Doing one or two of the swaps while keeping the others fresh/in stays in hamburger-loaf territory. All three together lands in the anglican register. This is the CORE CHASSIS the recipe is built on now.

5. FRESH CRUSHED GARLIC ADDED LATE. Realized the pie was missing a top-note bite — everything else was cooked or dried/powdered. Started crushing fresh garlic cloves and stirring them in AFTER the food processor step (not during the sauté) so the raw-garlic sharpness survives. The lingering raw edge carries the finished pie and reads well against the mushroom-cream base. Powdered garlic doesn't do this.

6. PUREED CELERY WITH THE MUSHROOMS. Tried pulsing ~2 stalks of celery into the food processor along with the mushrooms during the mushroom-chop step. Added real depth — celery brings a vegetal-savory bass note that supports the mushroom/walnut/miso stack without competing. Cross-check: the same pureed-mushroom + celery + lentil combination shows up in [[lentil-mushroom-potato-stew]], which suggests this is a stable pattern rather than a one-off.

7. BIGGEST UPGRADE — HEAVY CREAM HYDRATION. Started stirring 3-4 tbsp heavy cream into the filling after the food processor step, when it would otherwise be moldable-dry. Doesn't make the pie read creamy (pureed lentils are a powerful sponge — they absorb the cream), but adds real fat, keeps the filling from drying during the bake, and makes each bite read more SATISFYING. Single biggest quality upgrade to the dish.

8. FRENCH DIRECTION ALSO WORKS. Tried the same chassis with french seasonings instead of anglican — DIJON MUSTARD replacing worcestershire/tamarind as the depth-and-tang slot, TARRAGON alongside thyme. Equally good, just a different register. Realized the chassis (no tomato, powdered onion, dried herbs, butter, heavy cream, celery, late garlic) is neutral enough underneath that you can pull it anglican OR french without worrying about clashing between the two directions.

9. RESTRUCTURED AS POT PIE. The wellington format (form log → pre-bake → cool → thaw pastry → braid → re-chill → two-temp bake) is a project. Weeknight-scale execution: skip the log-forming/pre-bake steps entirely, transfer the filling straight into a pie plate under a single crust (or panko topping), bake at 400°F for ~30 min. Same filling, much less production. This is where the recipe landed as its own thing worth naming separately from Nisha's original — different format, different modifications, different register.

The result: a pot pie that reads distinctly anglican or french (your pick) rather than contemporary-vegan, with a substantial meat-analog filling that stands alongside the classical roasts these formats descend from.

=== WHY POT PIE INSTEAD OF WELLINGTON ===

The wellington format is a project — form the log, pre-bake it, cool completely, thaw and roll the pastry, braid the pastry, re-chill, two-temperature bake. The pot pie format skips all of that: filling goes in a pie plate, single crust on top, one bake at 400°F for ~30 min. Weeknight-executable rather than holiday-project.

The filling is essentially the same umami architecture as [[lentil-wellington]]'s — mushroom + toasted walnut + miso + nutritional yeast + lentil-as-binder — so the flavor foundation is proven. What's different is the surrounding modifications (dried aromatics, no tomato, heavy cream, late garlic) and the format (pie plate, not braided pastry log).

=== HAZARD — WHY THE FRESH-TO-DRIED SWAPS BELONG TOGETHER (AVOID HAMBURGER-Y READ) ===

The THREE-WAY combination of FRESH DILL + TOMATO PASTE + FRESH DICED ONIONS pushes the loaf/pie into a distinctly hamburger-loaf-with-ketchup register — not the good burger-and-relish read, more like a diner meatloaf. Fine flavor in the abstract; wrong flavor for what this pie is trying to be.

The swaps in this recipe (onion powder, dried herbs, no tomato paste) are structured as a UNIT to avoid that register. Doing only one or two of the swaps while keeping the others fresh/in leaves you in hamburger-loaf territory. All three swaps together are what put the dish in an anglican or french register rather than a diner one.

IF YOU WANT TOMATO PASTE + FRESH ONION + FRESH ROSEMARY, that's [[lentil-wellington]] Nisha-by-the-book (in wellington OR pot pie format — the underlying filling works either way). This recipe is specifically the no-tomato / powdered-onion / dried-herbs build.

=== DIRECTIONAL PICKERS — ANGLICAN OR FRENCH (BOTH WORK) ===

On top of the core chassis, pick a flavor direction. Both work, and don't worry too much about clashing between them — there's a lot of variety here:

- ANGLICAN DIRECTION: worcestershire sauce and/or tamarind paste as the depth-and-tang slot (worcestershire is tamarind + anchovy + molasses + spices in one bottle; tamarind alone is the vegan cheat). DRIED DILL as the herb alongside thyme. Dill is at home in british / northern-european cooking.
- FRENCH DIRECTION: dijon mustard as the depth-and-tang slot (fermented mustard has the same umami-plus-tang function). DRIED TARRAGON alongside thyme. Tarragon is the french signature herb, and it pairs with the mustard.
- BLEND: mustard + worcestershire together is fine; tarragon + dill together is fine. The mushroom/walnut/miso base is neutral enough underneath to hold either or both.

=== BIGGEST UPGRADE — HEAVY CREAM HYDRATES THE FILLING ===

Stir 3-4 tbsp HEAVY CREAM into the filling AFTER the food processor step, when it would otherwise be moldable-dry.

What this DOESN'T do: make the filling read creamy. The pureed lentils are a powerful sponge — they absorb the cream and the finished pie doesn't taste creamy at all.

What this DOES do: adds a lot of fat, keeps the filling from drying out during the 30-min bake, and makes the whole pie read more SATISFYING — richer per bite. This was the single biggest upgrade I found; the difference between with-cream and without-cream is real.

=== FRESH GARLIC IS REQUIRED — CRUSHED, ADDED LATE ===

Unlike the wellington version (where garlic can cook with the mushrooms and soften), this pie wants CRUSHED fresh garlic added LATE so it keeps some BITE. Crush the cloves (side of a knife or a garlic press), stir them into the filling after the food processor step — not during the mushroom sauté. The lingering raw-garlic sharpness carries the finished pie and reads well against the mushroom-cream base.

Powdered garlic doesn't do this — the raw-crushed edge is what matters. This is the one aromatic that stays fresh in this recipe (everything else — onion, dill/tarragon — goes powdered or dried).

=== PUREED CELERY WITH THE MUSHROOMS ===

Pulse ~2 stalks of celery into the food processor along with the mushrooms during the mushroom-chop step. Celery brings a vegetal-savory bass note that supports the mushroom/walnut/miso stack without competing. Not the crunchy-celery register; the pureed celery disappears into the background and just makes the filling read more layered.

Cross-reference [[lentil-mushroom-potato-stew]] — pureed mushrooms + celery + lentils appear together there too. That whole flavor architecture is a stable french-vegan-comfort-food combination worth remembering.

=== TOASTED WALNUTS ARE THE ONLY VALID NUT (SAME RULE AS LENTIL WELLINGTON) ===

Same rule as [[lentil-wellington]]: TOASTED walnuts, no substitutions. Almonds MAKE IT WORSE (sweet-crunchy against savory-earthy — clashing). Raw untoasted walnuts MAKE IT WORSE (take the umami slot without filling it; mute surrounding aromatics without contributing). See lentil-wellington's TOASTED WALNUTS section for the full argument.

=== POT PIE FORMAT NOTES ===

See [[turnip-yam-pie]] for the pot pie format details (single-crust pie plate, egg wash, vents, 400°F ~30 min bake, or panko-topping alternative with oil spray). Same format applies here — just a different filling.

The heavy cream in this filling means you probably don't need a separate gravy component (unlike [[turnip-yam-pie]] which builds a bouillon gravy in-pan). The filling is moist enough on its own.

=== CROSS-REFERENCE: [[lentil-mushroom-potato-stew]] ===

The french direction of this pie has heavy DNA overlap with [[lentil-mushroom-potato-stew]] (pureed mushrooms + dijon mustard + lentils + celery). That stew is basically the french direction of this filling, minus the pastry. If you like this pie french, you'll probably like that stew — and vice versa.

=== MISO + NUTRITIONAL YEAST HERE IS A LEGITIMATE WIN ===

Miso + nutritional yeast is the classic 'vegan glutamate bomb' — a shortcut I'm generally critical of when it's the whole umami stack. It's fine here because it sits inside a broader flavor architecture: toasted walnuts (roasty), mushrooms (glutamate + texture), fermented condiments (worcestershire OR mustard, tangy + deep), dried herbs (woodsy), lemon juice (bright), pureed celery (vegetal bass), late crushed garlic (bite). Miso + nooch add depth to that stack rather than substituting for it. See [[feedback_vegan_glutamate]] for the general principle: bad as the WHOLE umami stack; good as part of a broader one.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[lentil-wellington]]: Nisha's by-the-book original — same umami base, wellington log-in-braided-pastry format, fresh onion + tomato paste + fresh rosemary (the contemporary-vegan register).
- [[turnip-yam-pie]]: pot pie format specifics (single crust or panko topping, egg wash, vents, bake temp/time). Different filling entirely (turnips + sweet potatoes) but same pot-pie skeleton.
- [[lentil-mushroom-potato-stew]]: same lentil + mushroom + mustard + celery DNA as the french direction, but in stew form.
original_chef: Adapted from Nisha Vora's Lentil Wellington (Rainbow Plant Life). Restructured as a pot pie with a load-bearing set of swaps: onion powder for fresh onion, dried herbs (dill or tarragon) for fresh rosemary, no tomato paste (worcestershire/tamarind or dijon mustard instead), butter for olive oil, heavy cream to hydrate the filling, pureed celery pulsed with the mushrooms, fresh crushed garlic added late for bite.
